traveler: Antoinette de Saint Léger (born Bayer or Tzikos; styled Baroness de Saint Léger)
title: Two Rocks in Lago Maggiore: the Baroness of Brissago, the Garden Carried Over by Boat, and the Poorhouse at Intragna
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Saint Petersburg: the Name in Dispute

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the birth on the Neva
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and the city (de.wikipedia, 'Antoinette de Saint Léger'). The coordinate is the Winter Palace, standing for the imperial city and not for any documented birth site. The surname is contested: de.wikipedia gives Bayer (elsewhere Beyer), fr.wikipedia gives Tzikos, and neither is documented against a register. Silvano Pezzoli's ticino.ch note hedges even the city, writing «peut-être à Saint-Pétersbourg».
stops.campa: On the twentieth of June a girl is born in Saint Petersburg. The German record calls her Bayer; the French record calls her Tzikos. She will spend ninety-one years under a third name that belongs to an Irish house she marries into, and a title that house has no right to. The city gives her a birthday and withholds everything else: no register, no parish, no parents named twice the same way. No consulted source disputes the date. Everything on either side of it is a choice between two records.
stops.quote: Cette femme intelligente et cultivée, à la vie aventureuse et aux nombreuses amours, naît en 1856 (peut-être à Saint-Pétersbourg).
stops.quote_source: Silvano Pezzoli, biographical note for ticino.ch, reproduced at stleger.info/annonces/baronne.htm; modern promotional text, not a lifetime document
suggested_refs: The GND authority record 137493398 and the Deutsche Biographie entry, the only authority-file trace of her name

stops.name: Smolny Institute, the piano
stops.date_confidence: attested that she attended the Smolny Institute and studied piano, later under Liszt (de.wikipedia). No year is given by any consulted source; 1866 is a placeholder inside a plausible schooling age. The coordinate is the Smolny Institute building. Where and when the Liszt tuition happened is an open gap, and the research pool wrongly relocated this whole education to Naples.
stops.campa: The Smolny Institute schools the daughters of the empire, and she learns piano in it. Later, the German record says, she studies under Liszt, though no source names the city or the year of that tuition. It is the only education anyone attributes to her, and its two halves do not connect: an institute in Petersburg that nobody dates, a teacher somewhere else that nobody places. Nothing survives of what she played, then or in the sixty years afterward on a lake at the other end of Europe.
suggested_refs: The Smolny Institute for Noble Maidens, Saint Petersburg

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the forty-eight hours
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Tradition holds she was an illegitimate daughter of Tsar Alexander II and was ordered out of Russia within forty-eight hours (en.wikipedia, hedged twice: 'believed to be', 'said to have been'). No primary document is named by anyone in any language. The year 1869 is a placeholder set before the Naples placement and the attested 1873 Portici marriage; no consulted source dates the expulsion at all.
stops.campa: The story every language edition repeats, and none of them documents, is that her father is the tsar. Alexander II, the emancipator, who will be blown apart by a bomb on a Petersburg embankment in 1881. The story adds a deadline: forty-eight hours to leave Russia. English Wikipedia says 'believed to be' and 'said to have been'; the Zurich Joyce scholarship says 'supposedly'. Every teller hedges and every teller tells it. She is sent south, and she never comes back to this river.
stops.quote: The Baroness Antonietta de Saint-Léger (1856–1948), supposedly an illegitimate daughter of Tsar Alexander II, was an extravagant lady who lived on the Brissago Islands near Locarno.
stops.quote_source: Andreas Fischer, '2.41 Baroness Antonietta de Saint-Léger', in James Joyce in Zurich (Springer, 2020), pp. 207-210, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-51283-5_45; abstract verified verbatim on two hosts, chapter body paywalled and unread
suggested_refs: The unproven Romanov parentage, repeated in four language editions without a primary document
sources: Andreas Fischer, James Joyce in Zurich (2020)

stops.name: Naples, sent south for the lungs
stops.date_confidence: attested that she was sent to Naples 'for health rehabilitation and to learn Italian' (en.wikipedia, verbatim), placed there with a governess. No year is given; 1870 is a placeholder before the attested 1873 marriage. The coordinate is the city, not a documented address. The research pool's plural, 'languages', is corrected here against the source text.
stops.campa: She is placed in Naples with a governess, sent for the air and for the language. English Wikipedia gives the reason in five words: health rehabilitation, and to learn Italian. Italian is the tongue she will keep house in for the next seventy-eight years, on a Swiss lake that speaks it and in the Centovalli poorhouse where she dies speaking it. No source gives the year she arrives, the name of the governess, or the district she is lodged in. She does not go back to Russia.
suggested_refs: The Neapolitan foreign colony of the 1870s, into which she is placed by her father's representative

stops.name: Portici, the marriage to the consul general
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year, the place and the husband by de.wikipedia, verbatim: «1873 heiratete sie in erster Ehe in Portici bei Neapel den deutschen Generalkonsul Friedrich Stolte († 1878).» No month or day is given. The geography lens claimed his name appears in no consulted source; that claim is false and is corrected here, and the pin is moved the eleven kilometres from Naples to Portici.
stops.campa: At Portici, eleven kilometres down the coast from Naples under Vesuvius, she marries Friedrich Stolte, consul general of Germany. She is seventeen. The English record of her life leaves this husband nameless; the German record names him, dates the wedding, and marks his death five years off. A consul general is an office that issues papers for a living. Stolte's rank is the only one in her ninety-one years that a state actually conferred, and she holds it for five of them. For her own birth, her own parentage and the barony she signs after 1885 she never produces a document at all.
suggested_refs: The German consulate general at Naples in the 1870s, Friedrich Stolte's post

stops.name: Naples, the son of Giulio Ewald Jaeger
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the father by de.wikipedia, which records a son born of a union with Giulio Ewald Jaeger in 1876 while Friedrich Stolte is still living; Stolte dies 1878. No consulted source explains the overlap, and none gives a place, so the Naples coordinate is a placeholder. Flagged, not resolved.
stops.campa: A son is born, and the father named in the German record is not her husband. Giulio Ewald Jaeger, 1876; Friedrich Stolte does not die until 1878. No source consulted explains the two years in which both men stand in the same sentence. No second marriage is dated, no separation recorded. The German article states the birth in one clause and moves on to the next decade, and the son is never mentioned again by anybody in any language. The overlap is left standing here the way the source leaves it.
suggested_refs: The 1876 birth recorded in de.wikipedia, unexplained against the 1873 marriage and the 1878 death

stops.name: Naples, the widow marries the Anglo-Irishman
stops.date_confidence: attested for both years by de.wikipedia: Stolte dies 1878, she marries Richard Fleming in 1881. Neither event is given a place by any consulted source; the Naples coordinate is a placeholder drawn from the fact that she is living there. The surname appears variously as Fleming, Flemyng, and Fleming de Saint Léger.
stops.campa: Stolte dies in 1878. Three years later she marries Richard Fleming, an Anglo-Irish officer whom some sources also make a banker, and whose name they cannot spell the same way twice: Fleming, Flemyng, Fleming de Saint Léger. No source names the church or the city. What he brings is an inheritance from an uncle and a set of titles the uncle is said to have held. She takes up the titles before anyone checks the inheritance. She is twenty-five, and four years from owning two islands outright.
suggested_refs: The Fleming family inheritance, the money that buys the Brissago Islands four years later

stops.name: Doneraile, the title that is not there
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction on the title, attested on the style. de.wikipedia says Fleming bore, after an uncle's death, «die - angeblich von Wilhelm dem Eroberer verliehenen - Titel eines Grafen von Doneraile und Barons von Saint Léger»; angeblich means allegedly, and en.wikipedia drops the hedge. Doneraile is in fact a Viscountcy in the Peerage of Ireland, held across 1885-1941 by Hayes St Leger (d. 1887), Richard Arthur St Leger (d. 1891) and Edward St Leger (1866-1941). No Richard Fleming appears in the succession. The date and coordinate mark the claim, not a visit; nothing places her in Ireland.
stops.campa: In County Cork there is a Doneraile, and it carries a Viscountcy in the Peerage of Ireland, and across the years in question three men hold it in turn, none of them named Fleming. The claim Fleming brings out of his uncle's estate is a countship of Doneraile and a barony of Saint Léger, granted, the story says, by William the Conqueror. The German record prints the word angeblich, allegedly, and the English record drops it. From 1885 onward she signs herself Baroness.
suggested_refs: The Peerage of Ireland succession to the Viscountcy of Doneraile, 1885-1941

stops.name: Isole di Brissago, the purchase
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the buyers (en.wikipedia, fr.wikipedia); no month is given. Coordinate corrected to the fr.wikipedia infobox fix 46.133025 / 8.735504, confirmed by it.wikipedia at 46°07'58"N 8°44'09"E; the research pool's 46.1338 / 8.7247 falls roughly 830 m WNW, in open water. The islands belong administratively to the commune of Brissago, not to Ronco sopra Ascona as the afterlife lens stated.
stops.campa: Two rocks in the Swiss end of Lago Maggiore, uninhabited, scrubbed over with whatever grows on stone. Fleming's inheritance buys them both: the larger, San Pancrazio, and the smaller, Sant'Apollinare, which the shore also calls the island of rabbits. There is no soil worth the name and no house that has held anybody in three hundred years. She is twenty-nine. She has bought the only piece of ground in her life that will belong to her outright, and it is barely ground.
suggested_refs: The 1885 conveyance of the Isole di Brissago, commune of Brissago, Ticino

stops.name: Isola di Sant'Apollinare, the Umiliati church
stops.date_confidence: attested that the ruins of the Umiliati church stand on the smaller island (it.wikipedia) and that the Umiliati house was suppressed by Pope Pius V in 1571, its property assigned to the hospital at Locarno (en, it and fr Wikipedia concur). No consulted source gives the smaller island a coordinate of its own; it shares the pair's single fix. The June date is a placeholder inside the purchase year.
stops.campa: On the smaller island stand the ruins of a church of the Umiliati, a thirteenth-century order whose house here was suppressed by Pius V in 1571 and whose property went to the hospital at Locarno. Three hundred and fourteen years of nobody. That is the interval she buys into. The stone shell has outlasted every person who could have said what the building was for, and no consulted source records anything standing between the suppression and her purchase. She will plant a botanical garden in the gap the order left.
suggested_refs: The Umiliati house on Sant'Apollinare, suppressed by Pope Pius V in 1571

stops.name: Isola Grande, the convent rebuilt into a house
stops.date_confidence: attested that the old convent building was rebuilt as their residence (en.wikipedia, fr.wikipedia); no month and no completion date is given, and September is a placeholder inside the purchase year. The two islands share one coordinate across all consulted sources, and no separate fix exists for the villa itself.
stops.campa: The convent walls come back up as a house. Fleming supervises the rebuilding; she supervises everything else. What rises is a house grafted onto a religious plan: cells become rooms, the cloister becomes a courtyard where a piano can stand out of the wind. No consulted source dates the completion of the work. Later she hangs the walls with painted scrolls of scenes from the Odyssey. A man writing a book about a man trying to get home by water will cross the lake to see them.
suggested_refs: The rebuilt Umiliati convent on Isola Grande, the Saint Léger residence 1885 to 1927

stops.name: Isola Grande, the soil arrives by boat
stops.date_confidence: attested for the work and its method by isoledibrissago.ti.ch and de.wikipedia, both of which date the planting from 1886 onward; the chronology lens dated it 1885, which the German and cantonal sourcing do not support. No month is given. The official park history page at isoledibrissago.ti.ch/it/storia/ returns HTTP 404, so this material reaches the atlas at one remove.
stops.campa: Everything the garden needs has to cross water. Soil in boats, plants in boats; the gardeners come the same way, morning and evening from Brissago on the shore. She lays paths. She plants eucalyptus and palms in ground that arrived by the ton in the bottom of a rowing boat. The lake keeps the frost off and the imported earth does the rest. Two rocks that carried scrub for three hundred years carry a subtropical garden instead. The work starts in 1886 and no consulted source gives it a month or an end.
suggested_refs: The Parco Botanico del Cantone Ticino, direct descendant of this 1886 planting

stops.name: Isola Grande, Ranzoni paints her
stops.date_confidence: attested that Daniele Ranzoni painted an oil portrait of her on the islands in 1886 (swissinfo.ch, 25 July 2017, which traces its later provenance). No month is given and June is a placeholder. Ranzoni dies in 1889, which is the outer bound on any visit of his.
stops.campa: Daniele Ranzoni comes over from the Italian shore and paints her in oil. He has three years left to live. The canvas he makes on this island will outlast her house, her marriage, her fortune and her name: sold by the Locarno bankruptcy office after her death, passed through the Giacomo Jucker collection into private Italian hands, carried back across the water in 2017 to hang in a room she never saw built. It is the only face the record keeps of her.
suggested_refs: Daniele Ranzoni's 1886 oil portrait of the baroness, painted on Isola Grande
sources: swissinfo.ch, Gerhard Lob, 'Il ritorno della «principessa» russa sulle Isole di Brissago', 25 July 2017

stops.name: Isola Grande, Filippo Franzoni on the water
stops.date_confidence: attested that Filippo Franzoni was among the painters received on the islands (en.wikipedia); no visit of his is dated by any consulted source. 1890 is a placeholder inside the attested 1886-1914 span and carries no evidentiary weight.
stops.campa: Filippo Franzoni of Locarno paints this lake his whole working life and dies in an asylum at Mendrisio. He is among the painters she receives. No source consulted dates a single one of his crossings, or says what he painted here, or whether he came once or fifty times. The German record calls the span from 1886 to 1914 die grosse Zeit, the great time, and hands over four names to fill twenty-eight years. Franzoni is one of the four. The atlas gives him a year because a map needs one.
suggested_refs: Filippo Franzoni (1857-1911), Locarnese landscape painter of Lago Maggiore

stops.name: Isola Grande, Segantini crosses
stops.date_confidence: attested that Giovanni Segantini was among the artists received on the islands before the First World War (en.wikipedia); no visit is dated. Segantini dies on the Schafberg above Pontresina in 1899, which is the outer bound. 1895 is a placeholder inside that bound.
stops.campa: Giovanni Segantini paints Alpine light at altitude and dies of peritonitis in a hut on the Schafberg at forty-one, with the third panel of his triptych unfinished. Before that he comes down to a subtropical garden on a warm lake and sits in it. The two facts are not usually put in the same sentence. The garden is nine years planted by then and already the reason people come. The English record puts him in her house and gives no year, so the atlas guesses one and says that it is guessing.
suggested_refs: Giovanni Segantini (1858-1899), among the pre-war guests named by en.wikipedia

stops.name: Naples, Fleming goes and does not come back
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by de.wikipedia and it.wikipedia, which give her financial dealings and her personal conduct as the cause; en.wikipedia softens this to his finding her too impetuous and adds that he took a diplomatic post at the British consulate. No month is given. The sources differ on motive, not on the fact or the year.
stops.campa: Twelve years after he bought her the islands, Richard Fleming withdraws to Naples and stays there. The German and Italian records say it was her money-handling and her conduct; the English record says he found her too impetuous and took a consular post. All three agree he does not return to the lake. She is forty-one, and from this year she runs the island by herself. The marriage is never dissolved. Neither of them is recorded as filing anything anywhere, and she goes on signing his name and his uncle's title for the rest of her life.
suggested_refs: The British consulate at Naples, Fleming's post after 1897

stops.name: Isola Grande, Leoncavallo at the piano
stops.date_confidence: attested that Ruggero Leoncavallo was among her guests on the islands (en.wikipedia); no visit is dated by any consulted source. 1900 is a placeholder inside the attested 1886-1914 span.
stops.campa: Ruggero Leoncavallo, who has already written Pagliacci and will never write anything to match it, comes to the island. She was taught piano at the Smolny Institute and, the German record says, later by Liszt. Nothing in any source describes what they played, or whether they played at all. The English article names him as a guest and stops there. Her own account of these years ran to more than sixty volumes of diary, and no institution has been found that holds them.
suggested_refs: The sixty-odd volumes of her personal diaries, known to have existed, present whereabouts unknown

stops.name: Brissago, the shore calls her la sirena
stops.date_confidence: attested that the nickname was current in Ticino (Gerhard Lob, swissinfo.ch, 25 July 2017, reporting it rather than sourcing it to an archival document). No date is given for when it attaches; June 1900 is a placeholder inside the great time. The coordinate is the shore village of Brissago, from which her gardeners and guests crossed.
stops.campa: From the village on the shore they call her la sirena, the siren. She is a foreign woman alone on a rock in the water, with a garden nobody can account for and a title nobody has checked, receiving painters by boat. Ticino gives her the name that fits: the thing in the lake that draws men over and does not give them back. The 2017 article that records the nickname records no document behind it. It is what the shore said, and the shore is what kept it.
stops.quote_source: Gerhard Lob, 'Il ritorno della «principessa» russa sulle Isole di Brissago', swissinfo.ch, 25 July 2017
suggested_refs: The village of Brissago, embarkation point for the island's gardeners and guests

stops.name: Isola Grande, the daughter rows away
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. en.wikipedia states, as a bare fact with no date and no surrounding chronology, that the couple's daughter left the island with a gardener's help, escaping by boat. No other consulted source mentions a daughter at all. The year 1905 is a placeholder with no evidentiary basis whatsoever.
stops.campa: One sentence in the English article, with no date attached to it and nothing before or after: the daughter leaves the island with the help of a gardener, by boat. No other source consulted knows there is a daughter. The word used is escaping. Whatever the house on the island was to live in, one person in it wanted out badly enough that the getting out was recorded and the reason was not. The atlas prints the sentence, invents the year, and says so here.
suggested_refs: The undated departure of the daughter, en.wikipedia's single unsupported sentence

segments.name: The Other End of the Lake

stops.name: Monti sopra Locarno, Engelmann's vegetarians
stops.date_confidence: attested from engelmann.journey.json, which dates the Monte Trinità settlement 1898-1920 and carries this canonical pin. No consulted source records any contact between Engelmann's settlement and Saint Léger; the stop marks proximity on the same shore, not a meeting.
stops.campa: On the hillside above Locarno, ten kilometres up the water from her islands, Engelmann founds a vegetarian settlement at Monte Trinità and keeps it running for twenty-two years. In 1917 he writes Der Uranische Staat there. Nothing in any consulted source puts him on her boat or her on his hill. Two projects of the same decade, on the same shore of the same lake, each built by somebody who left another country to build it, and no record that either knew the other was there.
suggested_refs: Monte Trinità above Locarno, Engelmann's vegetarian house, 1898-1920

stops.name: Munich, the founding meeting
stops.date_confidence: attested from ida_hoffmann.journey.json, which carries this canonical Munich pin and date for the founding meeting of the vegetarian cooperative that becomes Monte Verità. Saint Léger is not present and is not mentioned in any account of it; the stop marks the origin of the settlement that will occupy the other end of her lake.
stops.campa: In Munich, Ida Hofmann and Henri Oedenkoven convene the meeting that founds a vegetarian cooperative and sets it looking for land. She is not in the room and does not know the room exists. What is decided here will be built four kilometres from her garden, and for the next twenty-seven years the two ends of Lago Maggiore will each hold a colony of people who left somewhere else. No source draws a line between them. The atlas draws the lake and leaves the line off.
suggested_refs: The Munich founding meeting of the cooperative that becomes Monte Verità, October 1900

stops.name: Ascona, the hill bought from Alfredo Pioda
stops.date_confidence: attested from ida_hoffmann.journey.json, which carries this canonical Monte Verità pin and date for the purchase from the Ticinese theosophist-politician Alfredo Pioda. Pioda appears independently at census_real_persons_2026-08-02.md line 286. No consulted source records contact between Saint Léger and any of the purchasers.
stops.campa: Ida Hofmann and Oedenkoven buy the hill above Ascona from Alfredo Pioda, a Ticinese theosophist who sits in politics and thinks about monasteries for the enlightened. Fifteen years after Saint Léger bought two rocks in the same water, the lake acquires its second pole. Hers is a garden with a piano in it; theirs will be a sanatorium with no meat in it. Both are foreigners who bought Ticinese ground with money made somewhere else, four kilometres apart, and neither party is recorded as calling on the other.
suggested_refs: Monte Verità, bought from Alfredo Pioda in December 1900

stops.name: Monte Verità, Laban's summer on the hill
stops.date_confidence: attested from laban.journey.json, mary_wigman.journey.json, suzanne_perrottet.journey.json and elsa_gindler.journey.json, all of which carry this canonical pin and the July 1913 date. No consulted source connects any of them to Saint Léger.
stops.campa: Rudolf von Laban brings his dance farm up the hill for the summer. Mary Wigman and Suzanne Perrottet arrive in July, and Elsa Gindler is recorded at the same hill in the same year. Barefoot movement choirs on a slope above Ascona, in the season when the baroness four kilometres down the water is still receiving guests in a garden of imported species. Nobody crosses. The lake carries boats all summer and no source consulted puts one of them on that route.
suggested_refs: Laban's summer dance farm on Monte Verità, 1913-1917

segments.name: The War, and the Second Circle

stops.name: Locarno, Joyce at the Pension Daheim
stops.date_confidence: attested from james_joyce.journey.json, which carries this canonical Locarno pin and the 5 November 1917 arrival at the Pension Daheim after Ernst Sidler's iridectomy in Zurich. Saint Léger does not appear in the Joyce record until 1919; this stop marks his arrival on her shore, not a meeting.
stops.campa: James Joyce comes south to Locarno in November with a cut eye, stays until January, and works. He is ten kilometres up the shore from the islands and does not yet know there is a baroness on them. Hermann Hesse is being analysed in the same small neutral country, and the war is over the border and nowhere inside it. The Odyssey scrolls have been hanging on her wall for years. Eighteen months pass before anybody in Locarno thinks to mention them to him.
suggested_refs: The Pension Daheim, Locarno, Joyce's lodging from 5 November 1917

stops.name: Isola Grande, Rilke and Kessler after the war
stops.date_confidence: attested that Rainer Maria Rilke and Harry Graf Kessler are among her guests after the First World War (en.wikipedia), placed at 1918/1919 by the research pool. No individual visit is dated by any consulted source; January 1918 is a placeholder at the front of that range.
stops.campa: The second circle is smaller and later than the first. Rainer Maria Rilke and Harry Graf Kessler come out to the island after the war, thirty years after Ranzoni painted her here. She is past sixty. The garden is fully grown. Nothing in her own hand survives to say what was said: the sixty volumes of diary covering these years are unaccounted for, and the one archive holding of her writing anywhere is a bundle of letters to a man neither of these two knew.
suggested_refs: Harry Graf Kessler's diaries, which run continuously through these years

stops.name: Minusio, Hesse settles on the same water
stops.date_confidence: attested from hermann_hesse.journey.json, which carries this canonical pin and date for his permanent arrival in Ticino; he had climbed Monte Verità in 1907. No consulted source records contact between Hesse and Saint Léger.
stops.campa: Hermann Hesse comes to Minusio in April and does not leave Ticino again. He climbed Monte Verità in 1907 and found it not quite the thing; now he settles a few kilometres along the shore and stays for the rest of his life. From this year the same stretch of water holds Hesse at one end, the baroness on her islands at the other, Engelmann's vegetarians on the hillside between, and Joyce in a Locarno pension writing about a man trying to get home by sea.
suggested_refs: The Minusio arrival of April 1919, and the 1907 climb up Monte Verità

stops.name: Locarno, the report of the Odyssey scrolls
stops.date_confidence: attested that Joyce, in Locarno and at work on Ulysses, learned that the baroness kept wall scrolls painted with scenes from the Odyssey (en.wikipedia); Art Ascona dates the visit to May 1919. Coordinate corrected to the canonical Locarno pin 46.1712 / 8.7994; the geography lens gave 46.1667 / 8.8, some 600 m out toward the water. That lens also called her sixty-three: born 20 June 1856, she is sixty-two in May 1919 and turns sixty-three only the following month.
stops.campa: Somebody in Locarno tells Joyce that the woman on the Brissago islands has the Odyssey painted on her walls. He is in the middle of writing a book that is the Odyssey. He is thirty-seven and half blind; she is sixty-two, four weeks short of sixty-three, and eight years from bankruptcy. The scrolls have been hanging on that island since before he was published. The whole of the meeting that follows turns on a piece of gossip about interior decoration.
suggested_refs: Art Ascona's dating of the Joyce visit to May 1919

stops.name: Isola Grande, Joyce takes the trunk
stops.date_confidence: attested that Joyce visited her on the islands in 1919 (en.wikipedia) and that he accepted from her a trunk of erotic books and letters intended for the writing of Circe (University of Oxford Figshare record 22892909, credited to William Brockman). The HTML page returns 403 and the record was read through the Figshare API; the research pool's guess that the claim traced to Budgen or Ellmann is dropped, since the record credits Brockman. The mid-May day is a placeholder inside the month Art Ascona gives.
stops.campa: Joyce crosses. He sees the scrolls. He leaves with a trunk of her erotic books and letters, which he means to use in the Circe episode, the night-town chapter where everything turns into something else. The Oxford record that preserves this transaction is a 403 in a browser and readable only through an interface for machines. So the record survives at an angle: a sixty-two-year-old baroness eight years from selling the islands hands the author of Ulysses a box of pornography, and the only catalogue entry for it is one a browser cannot open.
stops.quote: accepted from her a trunk of erotic books and letters, which he intended to use in the writing of "Circe"
stops.quote_source: 'Baroness St Leger', University of Oxford Figshare dataset record 22892909, credited to William Brockman; read via api.figshare.com/v2/articles/22892909 after the HTML page returned 403
suggested_refs: The Circe episode of Ulysses, for which the trunk was reportedly intended
sources: University of Oxford Figshare record 22892909 (William Brockman)

stops.name: Isola Grande, Transcaucasian railways and Romanian trams
stops.date_confidence: attested that she lost her fortune through speculative investments, named across sources as Transcaucasian railway shares and Romanian tram companies (de.wikipedia), compounded by failed business ventures (en.wikipedia, fr.wikipedia). No consulted source dates the purchases; 1920 is a placeholder inside the attested range of about 1918 to 1926.
stops.campa: The money goes into Transcaucasian railway shares and Romanian tram companies. Both are bets that eastern Europe after the war will be a going concern, and both are wrong. The German record names the instruments; the English and French records name only the losses. Whatever she still had of Fleming's inheritance, and whatever the great time had not already put into imported soil and imported plants, is now in paper issued by states that are being redrawn while she holds it.
suggested_refs: Transcaucasian railway shares and Romanian tram stock, the named instruments of her ruin

stops.name: Isola Grande, the dolls of famous beauties
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, though the source is better than the research pool claimed. de.wikipedia states it verbatim: «Sie stellte Puppen von berühmter Schönheit her.» The pool attributed this to an unnamed web summary; it is the same German article cited throughout. It stays [R] because no primary source and no holding collection has been located. The year is a placeholder inside the 1920s.
stops.campa: With no income she makes dolls and sells them, modelled, the German record says, on famous beauties. Six words in one encyclopaedia article and nothing beneath them: no photograph, no museum, no collector, no buyer named. A woman who imported a botanical garden by boat is now producing small figures of other women's faces for whatever the shore will pay. The claim is thin, and it is the only account anybody gives of how she fed herself in these years.
stops.quote: Sie stellte Puppen von berühmter Schönheit her.
suggested_refs: The ornamental dolls, unlocated in any museum or private collection

stops.name: Naples, Richard Fleming dies
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the place by de.wikipedia. No month or day is given by any consulted source. He has been in Naples twenty-five years by then and has not returned to the lake in any of them.
stops.campa: Twenty-five years after he walked out of the island house, Richard Fleming dies in Naples. She becomes a widow for the second time, and the titles she has been signing for thirty-seven years pass to nobody, because the succession they were claimed from ran through other men the whole time. The barony of Saint Léger dies in the same year as the man who claimed it, having existed only in the way she used it: as the name a lake knew her by. She keeps signing it.
suggested_refs: The 1922 death of Richard Fleming de Saint Léger at Naples

stops.name: Cannobio, the crossing no source names
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction on both the fact and the place. Only en.wikipedia reports that she used the islands as a base for smuggling goods between Italy and Switzerland; de.wikipedia, it.wikipedia, the isoledibrissago material and the 2017 swissinfo article carry no such claim. No source names a crossing point at all. Cannobio is the nearest Italian shore town and is placed here as an explicit reconstruction of a route, not an attested location. The year is a placeholder.
stops.campa: The English article, alone among the sources, says she ran goods across the border. The islands sit in Swiss water with the Italian shore a few kilometres off, which is a fact of geography, and smuggling is a plausible use for a private landing stage owned by somebody with debts. Plausible is all it is. No document, no customs record, no other language edition. Cannobio goes on the map here to mark a route nobody has attested, and this pin says as much.
suggested_refs: The Italian shore of Lago Maggiore opposite Brissago, unattested as any crossing point of hers

stops.name: Isole di Brissago, sold to Max Emden
stops.date_confidence: CONTRADICTION, recorded and not resolved. en.wikipedia gives 1926, in two places. de.wikipedia, it.wikipedia and fr.wikipedia all give 1927, and swissinfo.ch of 25 July 2017 is more precise still: «fine 1927», the end of the year. The atlas heads the stop 1927 on the weight of three language editions plus the news article, and records the English outlier here. No month is given by the majority sources.
stops.campa: Max Emden, department-store magnate of Hamburg and collector of art, buys the islands from her. She has owned them forty-two years. He will clear what is not useful and raise a villa of twenty-four rooms where the Umiliati house stood and where she rebuilt it. The English record dates the sale 1926 and the German, Italian and French records date it 1927; the Ticino press says the end of 1927. The atlas prints 1927 and leaves the disagreement standing.
suggested_refs: Villa Emden, the 24-room house Max Emden raises on Isola Grande after the purchase

stops.name: Casa Moscia, Ascona, the first room ashore
stops.date_confidence: attested that she relocated to Casa Moscia in Ascona after the sale (de.wikipedia); no month is given and June is a placeholder inside the year. The coordinate is the canonical Ascona-Moscia pin already carried by jung.journey.json, ida_hoffmann.journey.json, engelmann.journey.json and arnold_rikli.journey.json for the Eranos house, which stands on the same shore strip.
stops.campa: She moves to Casa Moscia, on the Ascona shore, four kilometres from the water she has just sold. Seventy-one years old, twice widowed, and for the first time in forty-two years a tenant. Moscia is a narrow strip between the hillside and the lake. Six years after she arrives, Olga Fröbe-Kapteyn will open a conference table on this same shore and the century's mythographers will start coming to it every August. No source consulted puts her at that table.
suggested_refs: Casa Moscia, Ascona, her residence from 1927

stops.name: Ascona, Weidemeyer raises the Teatro San Materno
stops.date_confidence: attested from charlotte_bara.journey.json, which carries this canonical pin and date. Bara has lived at Ascona since 1920 and danced at Locarno's Festa delle Camelie in 1924. No consulted source records any contact between Bara and Saint Léger, who is by then living a kilometre and a half away.
stops.campa: Carl Weidemeyer builds a theatre in Ascona for Charlotte Bara to dance sacred dance in. Bara has been on this shore since 1920, and in 1924 she danced at Locarno's Festa delle Camelie, a flower festival grown out of the same camellia culture that made the Brissago gardens famous. The woman who planted those gardens is now living a kilometre and a half from the new theatre with no money and no islands. Nothing in the record connects the two of them.
suggested_refs: The Teatro San Materno, Ascona, built 1928 by Carl Weidemeyer

stops.name: Ascona-Moscia, the Eranos table opens
stops.date_confidence: attested from jung.journey.json, ida_hoffmann.journey.json, engelmann.journey.json and arnold_rikli.journey.json, all of which carry this canonical pin and the 7 August 1933 date for the first Eranos Tagung. Saint Léger is living on this shore at the time and appears in no Eranos record consulted.
stops.campa: Olga Fröbe-Kapteyn opens the first Eranos Tagung at Moscia, on the shore below Monte Verità. Carl Gustav Jung lectures from that first year and will keep coming for decades. The baroness is seventy-seven and living on the same strip of shore, six years out of her islands, making dolls. The scholars of myth assemble a few hundred metres away to discuss the great mother and the descent into the underworld. No list of attendance consulted has her name on it.
suggested_refs: The first Eranos Tagung, Ascona-Moscia, 7 August 1933

stops.name: Intragna, the San Donato home
stops.date_confidence: attested for the month and the destination by de.wikipedia: she enters the San Donato nursing home at Intragna in November 1940, the home having opened in 1929. Coordinate corrected to de.wikipedia's Intragna TI fix, 46°10'39"N 8°42'00"E = 46.1775 / 8.7000, elevation 369 m; the geography lens gave 46.183 / 8.7 and the afterlife lens 46.1667 / 8.6931, out by about 600 m and 1.2 km respectively.
stops.campa: In November she goes up into the Centovalli, to the San Donato home at Intragna, three hundred and sixty-nine metres above the lake she spent half her life on. Europe is at war again. She is eighty-four. The islands are twelve kilometres away and out of sight behind the hill, and their owner Max Emden dies this same year, so that his son inherits what she sold. She will spend seven years and two months in this village, and she will die in it without leaving it again.
suggested_refs: The San Donato home at Intragna, opened 1929

stops.name: Intragna, the interview before the end
stops.date_confidence: attested that the sentence and the headline exist and were read verbatim in Gerhard Lob's swissinfo.ch article of 25 July 2017, which attributes them to a Corriere della Sera interview given shortly before her death. The Corriere issue itself was NOT located, so verification stops one remove short of the newspaper: [A] for the swissinfo citation, [R] for the ultimate Corriere wording. December 1947 is a placeholder for 'shortly before her death'.
stops.campa: A journalist from the Corriere della Sera comes up to the poorhouse and prints what she says. The headline he files is from the court of the tsar to the poorhouse of the poor. She is ninety-one, on public charity, in a village in the Centovalli, and what she gives him is the future tense. The atlas can reach the 2017 article that quotes the interview and cannot reach the interview. The sentence survives at one remove from the mouth that actually said it.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to her in a Corriere della Sera interview headlined 'Dalla corte dello Zar all'ospizio dei poveri', given shortly before her death; quoted in Gerhard Lob, swissinfo.ch, 25 July 2017. The Corriere issue itself was not located.
suggested_refs: The Corriere della Sera interview 'Dalla corte dello Zar all'ospizio dei poveri', unlocated

stops.name: Intragna, death in the poorhouse
stops.date_confidence: attested by de.wikipedia, fr.wikipedia and the GND authority record 137493398; swissinfo.ch describes her dying 'in the poorhouse at Intragna'. Age corrected: born 20 June 1856, died 24 January 1948 is 91 years and 7 months, so 91 is the figure consistent with the birth year and the 92 given in some retellings, and in the research pool, is the wrong one.
stops.campa: She dies on the twenty-fourth of January, ninety-one years and seven months old, in the poorhouse at Intragna. Some accounts say ninety-two; the arithmetic says ninety-one. She has outlived Fleming by twenty-six years, Ranzoni by fifty-nine, Segantini by forty-nine, and the ownership of her islands by twenty-one. The garden is still growing on them. Nobody at Intragna is recorded as knowing what it was she planted there, or what that planting is going to become.
suggested_refs: GND authority record 137493398 and the Deutsche Biographie entry

segments.name: Afterlife: the Portrait, the Garden, the Transfer

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the letters to Leon Hirsch
stops.date_confidence: attested that correspondence from Antoinette de Saint Léger to Leon Hirsch survives in the Deutsches Exilarchiv within the Leon Hirsch Nachlass, catalogued via Archivportal-D. The catalogue entry is UNDATED; 1933, the year German exile begins, is a placeholder with no evidentiary basis. The pin marks an archive shelf and not her movement: she is at Ascona in 1933 and is not recorded as ever going to Frankfurt, and the stop opens the afterlife segment because what it locates is what outlived her. This is the only located archival trace of her own writing, and it is unpublished and untranslated.
stops.campa: In the German Exile Archive at Frankfurt, inside the papers of Leon Hirsch, there is correspondence from her. It is the only writing in her own hand that any archive consulted admits to holding: not the sixty volumes of diary, not a letter to Rilke or Kessler or Joyce, one bundle addressed to one exiled German writer. It is undated in the catalogue, unpublished and untranslated. Everything else anybody knows about her comes from people describing her from the outside.
suggested_refs: Deutsches Exilarchiv, Nachlass Leon Hirsch, correspondence from Antoinette de Saint Léger

stops.name: Locarno, the bankruptcy office sells the estate
stops.date_confidence: attested that her estate, including Ranzoni's 1886 portrait, was auctioned by the Locarno bankruptcy office after her death, the portrait then passing through the Giacomo Jucker collection into a private Italian collection (swissinfo.ch, 25 July 2017). No date is given for the auction; June 1948 is a placeholder after the January death. The coordinate is the canonical Locarno pin.
stops.campa: The bankruptcy office at Locarno sells what is left. Among the lots is the Ranzoni: the oil portrait painted on her island in 1886, when the garden was one year in the ground and she was thirty. It goes into the Giacomo Jucker collection and from there into private Italian hands. Her sixty volumes of diaries appear in no account of the sale, and no institution has been found that holds them. She died at Intragna in January on public charity, and what the office is auctioning it is auctioning for debt.
suggested_refs: The Locarno bankruptcy office auction of her estate, 1948

stops.name: Isole di Brissago, sold to the consortium
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the price by de.wikipedia («1949 für rund 700'000 Franken») and for the buyer by it.wikipedia, which names «un consorzio che comprendeva il Canton Ticino, i comuni di Ascona, Brissago e Ronco sopra Ascona». The research pool said the Canton bought alone, which it.wikipedia contradicts; full cantonal ownership comes only in 2019. No month is given.
stops.campa: A year after she dies, Hans Erich Emden sells the islands his father bought from her. The buyer is not one owner but four: the Canton of Ticino together with the communes of Ascona, Brissago and Ronco sopra Ascona, for about seven hundred thousand francs. The garden opens to the public. What she made as a private obsession on ground she owned outright becomes a thing held in common, and the canton alone will not hold full title to any of it until 2019.
suggested_refs: The 1949 consortium purchase and the 2019 transfer of full title to the Canton of Ticino

stops.name: Isola Grande, the remains carried back
stops.date_confidence: attested by fr.wikipedia, 'Îles de Brissago', verbatim: «Sa dépouille fut ensuite transférée sur la Grande île le 12 août 1972.» This directly contradicts the afterlife lens, which recorded an explicit gap and said no source names a grave. The transfer is attested and the gap is not, so the atlas carries the transfer. Where she lay between 1948 and 1972 is a genuine open gap that no consulted source fills.
stops.campa: Twenty-four years and seven months after she dies at Intragna, her remains are carried back across the water to the larger island. She had owned it, planted it, lost it, and died twelve kilometres away from it on public charity. Where she lay in the meantime, no source consulted says. The transfer is the last event in her life story and it happens a generation after her life. The ground she is in now is ground she paid for and did not keep, and it is a public park.

stops.name: Villa Emden, the portrait comes home
stops.date_confidence: attested by swissinfo.ch, 25 July 2017: the Ranzoni portrait is exhibited in the Sala Rossa of Villa Emden on the larger Brissago island from July to mid-October 2017, an initiative of the Galleria Maspes of Milan (Elena Orsenigo). The exact opening day is not given; 1 July is a placeholder inside the stated run.
stops.campa: Ninety years after the sale, the Ranzoni is brought back and hung in the Sala Rossa of Villa Emden, in the house the man who bought her out built on the site of the house she built. The Galleria Maspes of Milan arranges it, and the exhibition runs to mid-October. The article that reports it calls her the Russian princess in quotation marks, because nobody has ever proved she was one. The portrait spends three months on the island and then goes back into private hands.

stops.name: Isole di Brissago, the Parco Botanico
stops.date_confidence: attested by it.wikipedia for the present-day figures, roughly 1,700 plant species and over 90,000 visitors a year, and for the 2019 passage of full ownership to the Canton of Ticino. The closing quotation is modern tourism text, an ha-sen.de note in Nathalie's French translation reproduced at stleger.info; it is a secondary paraphrase and not a period document, and is flagged as such.
stops.campa: The Canton takes full title in 2019. The garden she began by rowing soil across in 1886 now holds something like seventeen hundred species and takes more than ninety thousand visitors a year. She has no statue on it and no plaque. The parentage that gave her a story was never documented, and the barony was never conferred. The diaries are gone, and the park's own history page returns a 404. What she has instead is a working institution that nobody entering it needs to know her name in order to use.
stops.quote: L'Ile abrite aujourd'hui le Jardin botanique du canton du Tessin, dont l'âme, indiscutablement, est Antoinette de Saint-Léger.
